mainTopic: Which growth stage sets a crop's year for מעשרות and שביעית: the שליש derivation, the השרשה rule for rice, millet, poppy, and sesame, and the debate over בילה (mixing) and שמואל's rule of גמר פרי
overview: This amud first finishes the גמרא's proof that grain belongs to the year in which it reached one-third (שליש) of its growth. The proof rereads לשלש in the פסוק as לשליש, and a second פסוק covers the plain three-year promise. Next comes a משנה: rice, millet, poppy, and sesame are assigned to a year by when they took root (השרשה). רבה notes that this matches none of the standard rules: trees follow חנטה, grain and olives follow שליש, and vegetables follow לקיטה. He explains that these crops ripen little by little, so the חכמים used rooting to keep the whole field in one year. אביי challenges him from a ברייתא of רבי שמעון שזורי: the farmer could simply pile the harvest together and tithe from the mixture. רבה answers that רבי שמעון שזורי holds יש בילה, while the חכמים hold אין בילה. שמואל rules like רבי שמעון שזורי, and רבי זירא objects that שמואל himself says solids do not mix. The גמרא answers that for שמואל everything follows גמר פרי, so all the beans belong to one year anyway, without needing mixing.

steps.title: Reading the verse as 'one-third' instead of 'three'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof from the פסוק by rereading לשלש (for three) as לשליש (for one-third). This shows that grain's year is set when it reaches a third of its growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not read it as 'for three,' but as 'for one-third.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it started on the previous amud. It rereads one word in the פסוק so that it hints at the 'one-third' rule for grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the sixth-year crop will grow 'לשלש השנים' (for three years). By reading לשלש as לשליש, the גמרא finds a hint that grain counts toward the year in which it reached one-third of its growth. This tells us which year's מעשר rules apply to that grain.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as... but as (a rereading of a word in a פסוק to find a hint)

steps.confusionAlert: An אל תקרי reading does not mean the פסוק is spelled differently. The written text stays the same, and the rereading is only a hint used for the דרשה.

phrases.english: Do not read 'for three,'
phrases.notes: From Leviticus 25:21: 'and it shall bring forth produce for three years.'

phrases.english: but rather 'for one-third.'
phrases.notes: Same letters, different vowels. This hints at one-third growth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation the גמרא began on the previous amud with the פסוק of the sixth-year blessing.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that grain's year for מעשרות follows the point when it reaches שליש (one-third) of its growth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Leviticus 25:21, 'ועשת את התבואה לשלש השנים,' reread as לשליש.

steps.title: Isn't the verse needed for its plain meaning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the פסוק is needed for its simple message: the sixth year's crop will last three years. If so, it cannot also be used for the 'one-third' hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this verse is needed for its own plain meaning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof it just made. It argues the פסוק is already busy teaching its plain meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of the פסוק is a promise: the sixth year will produce enough food for three years. The challenge is that if the words are needed for that promise, they are not free to teach a new הלכה about one-third growth.

phrases.english: But it is needed for itself!
phrases.notes: It is needed to teach that the sixth-year crop will last three years.

steps.kashyaTarget: Using לשלש to derive the שליש rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק whose words are needed for their plain message cannot also serve as a source for a new הלכה.

steps.title: Another verse already teaches the three-year promise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a different פסוק already teaches that the crop will last into the ninth year. That leaves the first פסוק free for the 'one-third' hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another verse is written: 'And you shall sow in the eighth year and eat from the old produce until the ninth year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a second פסוק that teaches the plain meaning instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leviticus 25:22 says the people will still eat old produce until the ninth year. That already teaches that the crop lasts three years (sixth, seventh, and eighth). So the extra words in the first פסוק are not needed for that point, and they can teach the שליש rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Grain belongs to the year in which it reached שליש (one-third growth). The source is לשלש reread as לשליש. This works because a different פסוק covers the three-year promise.

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
'And you shall sow in the eighth year
and you shall eat from the old produce
until the ninth year.'
phrases.notes: This shows the sixth-year crop lasts three years.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the plain meaning to another פסוק, which frees the first פסוק for the דרשה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first פסוק is the only source for the three-year promise, so it cannot also teach שליש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Leviticus 25:22 teaches the three-year promise, so Leviticus 25:21 is free to teach the שליש rule.

steps.title: משנה: rice, millet, poppy and sesame go by when they took root
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה from elsewhere. If these four crops took root before ראש השנה, they are tithed as the old year's crop and are permitted in שביעית. If not, they are forbidden in שביעית and are tithed as the next year's crop.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Rice, millet, poppy, and sesame that took root before ראש השנה are tithed according to the past year and are permitted in the seventh year. If not, they are forbidden in the seventh year and are tithed according to the coming year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting a משנה about four special crops. It is setting up a question that רבה will ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these four crops, the deciding moment is השרשה (taking root). It is not when the fruit forms, when the crop reaches a third of its growth, or when it is picked. Rooting before ראש השנה ties the crop to the outgoing year for both מעשרות and שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
They are tithed according to the past year

steps.confusionAlert: 'Permitted in שביעית' does not mean you may plant or work the field in שביעית. It means that crops that already took root before the seventh year began count as sixth-year produce, so they are not forbidden as שביעית produce.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets a fourth way of deciding a crop's year: rooting. That does not match any of the three standard rules, and this is what drives the rest of the sugya.

phrases.english: We learned there:
Rice, millet, poppy, and sesame
that took root before ראש השנה
are tithed according to the past year,
and are permitted in the seventh year.
And if not, they are forbidden in the seventh year,
and are tithed according to the coming year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It is related to the previous derivation because both deal with which growth stage sets a crop's year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rice, millet, poppy, and sesame are assigned to a year (for מעשרות and שביעית) based on whether they took root before ראש השנה.

steps.title: רבה lists the three standard growth-stage rules
steps.stepSummary: רבה repeats the known rules. A tree's fruit goes by חנטה (when the fruit forms). Grain and olives go by שליש (one-third growth). Vegetables go by לקיטה (when they are picked).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The חכמים said: A tree goes by the formation of its fruit, grain and olives go by one-third growth, and vegetables go by picking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה lists the three known categories as a setup for the question he is about to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each type of produce has a fixed moment that decides its year. רבה sets out the three rules so that we can see that the משנה's rule of השרשה (rooting) does not match any of them.

keyTerms.meaning: The first formation of the fruit

steps.whatToRemember: There are three standard rules. A tree follows חנטה, grain and olives follow שליש, and vegetables follow לקיטה.

phrases.english: Rabba said: The Sages said:
a tree follows the formation of its fruit,
grain and olives follow one-third growth,
a vegetable follows picking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets out the background rules needed to question the משנה in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tree: חנטה. Grain and olives: שליש. Vegetables: לקיטה.

steps.title: To which category did the חכמים match these four crops?
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks which of the three categories the חכמים matched rice, millet, poppy, and sesame to. Following השרשה (rooting) does not match any of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: These, to what did the חכמים equate them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks his question. The rule for these crops, rooting, does not fit any of the three known categories, so where do they belong?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses השרשה, which is a fourth standard that is not on the list. רבה wants to know which known category these crops were modeled on and why they get a rule of their own. רבה himself answers in the next step.

phrases.english: These, like what did the Sages equate them?
phrases.notes: This refers to rice, millet, poppy, and sesame.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the list in step 5 to question the rooting rule in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which category (tree, grain, or vegetable) the four crops were modeled on, given that their rule of השרשה matches none of them.

steps.title: רבה explains why the חכמים chose rooting
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers his own question. These crops ripen a little at a time, so the חכמים used השרשה as the deciding point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה then said: Since these crops ripen little by little, the חכמים went by the time of rooting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה returns to the question he asked in Step 6 and now gives his own answer. Rice, millet, poppy, and sesame ripen bit by bit, so the חכמים used rooting instead of picking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If these crops went by לקיטה (picking), one field would be split between two years, since some would be picked before ראש השנה and some after. People would mix them up and tithe from one year's crop for the other year's crop. השרשה happens at about the same time for the whole field, so the whole field counts as one year.

keyTerms.meaning: Then / again. Here it marks רבה coming back to answer his own question.
Little by little. The crop ripens and is gathered in stages.
They go after, meaning they follow this as the deciding factor.

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying these crops stop being a crop that needs tithing. He is only explaining why the חכמים picked a different point in time (rooting) to decide which year they belong to.

phrases.english: Rabba then said:
Since they ripen little by little,
phrases.notes: They ripen and are picked in stages over a long period.

phrases.english: the Sages went by the time of rooting.
phrases.notes: Rooting is uniform for the whole field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רבה himself raised in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים used השרשה for these four crops.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: These crops ripen in stages. Rooting keeps the whole field in one year, so nobody tithes across years by mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These crops go by השרשה because they ripen little by little.

steps.title: אביי suggests mixing the whole harvest instead
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה. There was no need for a special rule, because the farmer could pile everything together and tithe from the mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Let him pile the harvest into the middle of his threshing floor. Then he ends up separating תרומה from the new crop in it for the new crop in it, and from the old crop in it for the old crop in it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's reason. He offers a simpler solution that avoids the problem without changing the rule to rooting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's worry was that the farmer would tithe old crop for new crop. אביי says to mix all the produce well, then take תרומה from the mixture. Each part of the separated portion then covers its own matching year. So רבה's worry does not seem strong enough to justify a special rule.

keyTerms.meaning: His threshing floor, where the harvest is gathered
Separates תרומה (the portion given to the כהן)
The new crop (the new year's produce)
The old crop (the previous year's produce)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Let him pile his harvest into the middle of his threshing floor,
phrases.notes: He mixes all the produce together well.

phrases.english: and it turns out he separates teruma from the new crop in it
for the new crop in it,

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַיָּשָׁן שֶׁבּוֹ עַל הַיָּשָׁן שֶׁבּוֹ!
phrases.english: and from the old crop in it for the old crop in it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְיִצְבּוֹר גּוֹרְנוֹ לְתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבה gave in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason that the חכמים needed השרשה so people would not tithe across years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mixing the harvest already solves the problem, so no special rule was needed.

steps.title: A ברייתא about Egyptian beans rooted in two different years
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא to back up his idea. It begins with the case of פול המצרי, where part of the field rooted before ראש השנה and part rooted after.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it taught: רבי יוסי בן כיפר said in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי: If פול המצרי (Egyptian beans) was planted for its seeds, and some took root before ראש השנה and some took root after ראש השנה, one may not separate תרומה and tithes from this for that. This is because one may not separate תרומה and tithes from the new crop for the old, nor from the old crop for the new.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי supports his challenge with a ברייתא. This step lays out the problem the ברייתא deals with, and the next step shows how the ברייתא solves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is a crop where one field really is split between two years. The ברייתא states the basic rule: you may not tithe from one year's crop for the other year's crop. That is exactly the same problem רבה described.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it taught in a ברייתא? A formula for bringing a supporting source.
That he planted for its seeds, not to eat as a vegetable

phrases.english: Isn't it taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon Shezuri:
Egyptian beans that one planted for seed,
some of it took root before Rosh HaShana,
and some of it took root after Rosh HaShana,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין וּמְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: one may not separate teruma and tithes from this for that,
because one may not separate teruma and tithes
neither from the new crop for the old
nor from the old crop for the new.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support אביי's challenge in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that mixing the harvest solves the problem of tithing across years.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי בן כיפר in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי about פול המצרי.

steps.title: The ברייתא's solution is to mix the harvest
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's solution is exactly what אביי suggested. The farmer piles everything together and tithes from the mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: How should he act? He piles the harvest into the middle of his threshing floor. Then he ends up separating תרומה and tithes from the new crop in it for the new crop in it, and from the old crop in it for the old crop in it.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes אביי's proof. The ברייתא solves the split-year problem by mixing, not by making a new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא uses mixing for פול המצרי, the same fix should work for rice, millet, poppy, and sesame. That leaves רבה's reason for using השרשה looking unnecessary. רבה responds in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: How should he act? (What is the practical solution?)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה said the חכמים used השרשה so people would not tithe across years. אביי showed from a ברייתא that mixing the harvest already solves that problem, so רבה's reason is now under attack.

phrases.english: How should he act?
He piles his harvest into the middle of his threshing floor,
and it turns out he separates teruma and tithes

phrases.aramaic: מִן הֶחָדָשׁ שֶׁבּוֹ עַל הֶחָדָשׁ שֶׁבּוֹ,
phrases.english: from the new crop in it for the new crop in it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִן הַיָּשָׁן שֶׁבּוֹ עַל הַיָּשָׁן שֶׁבּוֹ.
phrases.english: and from the old crop in it for the old crop in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 9 by giving its solution, which matches אביי's suggestion.
steps.raayaObject: That mixing the harvest is an accepted way to avoid tithing across years.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the same ברייתא: צוֹבֵר גּוֹרְנוֹ לְתוֹכוֹ.

steps.title: רבה Rejects the Proof: It Depends on Whether Things Mix
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון שזורי, who holds יש בילה. The חכמים hold אין בילה, so they cannot use the 'pile it together' solution.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to אביי: Are you quoting רבי שמעון שזורי? רבי שמעון שזורי holds that piled-together produce gets fully mixed. But the חכמים hold that it does not get fully mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back against אביי's proof. He says the ברייתא only works for one opinion, and the חכמים disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'pile it together and tithe' solution only works if the old and new produce become evenly mixed. רבי שמעון שזורי believes they do (יש בילה), so each portion taken off has the right share of old and new. The חכמים believe they do not (אין בילה), so they needed a different rule: השרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing: whether items piled together become evenly blended
There is mixing: the pile is treated as evenly blended
There is no mixing: the pile is not treated as evenly blended
Are you saying? / Are you quoting?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה is denying what the ברייתא says. He agrees that the ברייתא says to pile everything together. He is only saying that this is one opinion (רבי שמעון שזורי), not the view of the חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי קָאָמְרַתְּ?
phrases.english: He (Rabba) said to him: Are you quoting Rabbi Shimon Shezuri?
phrases.notes: The ברייתא from step 9 was taught in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי סָבַר יֵשׁ בִּילָּה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri holds that there is mixing.
But the Rabbis hold that there is no mixing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 9-10 by limiting it to one opinion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ברייתא cannot challenge the חכמים, because it follows only רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי's solution assumes יש בילה. The חכמים, whose rule רבה was explaining, hold אין בילה.

steps.title: שמואל Rules Like רבי שמעון שזורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר נחמני reports in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר, who quoted רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows what רבי יוסי בן כיפר said in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling. שמואל says we follow רבי שמעון שזורי: in the bean case, you may pile everything together and tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first time the sugya gives a final ruling on the ברייתא's case. It also sets up the next step, because it looks like שמואל accepts יש בילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who reported רבי שמעון שזורי's view

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar,
who spoke in the name of Rabbi Shimon Shezuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the ברייתא just discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי: the farmer may pile all the beans together and tithe from them.

steps.title: רבי זירא: שמואל Says Solids Do Not Mix
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא objects. שמואל himself said there is no mixing for anything except wine and oil. So how could he rule like רבי שמעון שזורי, who relies on mixing?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged this: Did שמואל really say that? But שמואל said: Nothing mixes except wine and oil!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא points out an apparent contradiction between two statements of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון שזורי's reason is יש בילה. שמואל's other statement says solids like beans do not mix; only liquids do. So שמואל seems to contradict himself by following רבי שמעון שזורי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objected to this:
Did Shmuel really say this?
But didn't Shmuel say:

phrases.aramaic: לַכֹּל אֵין בִּילָּה, חוּץ מִיַּיִן וָשֶׁמֶן!
phrases.english: Nothing has mixing, except wine and oil!
phrases.notes: Liquids blend evenly; solids like beans do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון שזורי's ruling depends on יש בילה, but שמואל holds that solids have אין בילה. So it seems שמואל cannot accept רבי שמעון שזורי's ruling.

steps.title: Same Ruling, Different Reason: Everything Follows Final Ripening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי זירא forgot another rule of שמואל: the tithe year follows גמר פרי. All the beans finish ripening together, so they all count as the same year, and no mixing is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא forgot what שמואל said: Everything follows the final ripening of the fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. שמואל agrees with רבי שמעון שזורי's practical ruling, but not because of mixing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the year of tithing is set by גמר פרי, the final ripening, not by השרשה. All the beans ripen at the same time, so they all belong to one year. They can be tithed together, and שמואל never needs יש בילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ripening of the produce

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל agrees with רבי שמעון שזורי's ruling (pile the beans together and tithe), but for his own reason: everything follows גמר פרי, so all the beans belong to the same year. He still holds that solids have אין בילה.
steps.confusionAlert: Agreeing with a ruling is not the same as agreeing with its reason. שמואל accepts the result of רבי שמעון שזורי but rejects the reason of בילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: an אמורא can rule like a תנא in practice while basing the ruling on a completely different principle.

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Zeira) forgot this that Shmuel said:
Everything follows the final ripening of the fruit.
phrases.notes: Since all the beans ripen together, they all belong to the new year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reasoning: same practical ruling, based on a different principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון שזורי because he accepts יש בילה, which contradicts his other statement.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל rules this way because the year follows גמר פרי, and all the beans ripen together. Mixing is irrelevant, so there is no contradiction.
